name: tempd2_l8_collapse

phase_0.boundary_condition: outer adiabatic boundary that contains the system and defines its spatial extent

VINIT.justification: void state before any gradient or collapse process begins

TANCH.justification: closed boundary that contains the temperature field and prevents external interference

AFWD.justification: forward morphism representing heat flow from hot to cold regions during collapse

AREV.justification: reverse morphism representing temporary local ordering before complete collapse

CLINK.justification: sequential chaining of expansion and contraction phases in the collapse process

IMSCRIB.justification: self-reference of the field at each timestep, representing the system's own state

FSPLIT.justification: splits the temperature field into two regions: hot core and cold periphery at the collapse threshold

FFUSE.justification: reconstitutes the original temperature distribution from the bifurcated regions after the collapse cycle

EVALT.justification: affirmative state where collapse completes without fragmentation into a singular dense core

EVALF.justification: negative state where collapse overshoots and disrupts local thermal equilibrium

ENGAGR.justification: paradice where the system is both collapsed and not collapsed, held without resolution near the critical threshold

IFIX.justification: permanent irreversible measurement of the collapse timestep and final temperature profile

phase_2.fuse_result: initial uniform temperature field (reconstructed via reversible thermal exchange)

phase_3.void_description: undetermined temperature state (absolute zero or no field defined)
phase_3.true_description: temperature within stable collapse range (affirmative, success outcome)
phase_3.false_description: temperature outside stable collapse range (negative, failure outcome)
phase_3.both_description: superposition of stable and runaway collapse (paradice, held simultaneously at critical point)

steps.domain_action: initialize the temperature field with uniform distribution
define the adiabatic boundary that encloses the system
apply the critical bifurcation point, splitting the field into hot core and cold periphery
on T-arm, evaluate the hot core region for stable collapse conditions
propagate thermal gradient forward along the T-arm toward the core center
on F-arm, evaluate the cold periphery for runaway collapse conditions
apply reverse entropy-driven reordering along the F-arm to counteract breakdown
compose the forward and reverse arms sequentially via a compression cycle
force self-reference of the temperature field to anchor its identity
recombine the bifurcated arms to reconstruct the original uniform field
permanently record the collapse event timestep and final temperature profile

phase_5.compiler_frontend: thermodynamic integrator that translates thermal gradients into collapse instructions
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: heat flux and phonon exchange between core and periphery regions
phase_5.memory_mechanism: temperature lattice storing scalar values per grid point at each timestep
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: adaptive timestep controller that triggers bifurcation at critical threshold
phase_5.alfs_store: canonical collapse scenario dataset from previous simulations of tempd2_l8

phase_6.cycle_cost: thermal energy dissipated as uniform field is reconstructed
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: system in bifurcated state with distinct hot and cold regions
phase_6.post_cycle_state: system in original uniform state after recomposition
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — reversible thermal exchange in the model conserves entropy exactly
